transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m having a hard time staying focused on work. I’ll sit down with a stack of essays or a curriculum document intending to get through it, and ten minutes later I realize I’ve been staring at the same page, thinking about other things, and not really taking any of it in.
Roughly how long have you been noticing this difficulty with your focus?
It’s been noticeably worse for about 11 months, since the school changed the curriculum calendar and added the after-school planning meetings.
Looking back, did you have similar difficulties with focus or paying attention during your childhood or school years?

Yeah, I think so. Even in primary school, my report cards would say things like “bright but careless,” or that I didn’t finish work unless someone was keeping a close eye on me. My parents also used to find crumpled-up worksheets in my backpack that I’d forgotten to hand in.
Over the past few months, have you been feeling persistently down, sad, or hopeless?
I’m not sure I’d say persistently, no. I get frustrated with myself sometimes, but I haven’t really felt down or hopeless most days.
Do you find yourself struggling with persistent, excessive worry or anxiety about everyday matters?
Not really. I do worry about things sometimes, like anyone, but I wouldn’t say it’s persistent or excessive.
